name: Maximum Sum on Even Positions
description: You are given an array $$$a$$$ consisting of $$$n$$$ integers. Indices of the array start from zero (i. e. the first element is $$$a_0$$$, the second one is $$$a_1$$$, and so on). You can reverse at most one subarray (continuous subsegment) of this array. Recall that the subarray of $$$a$$$ with borders $$$l$$$ and $$$r$$$ is $$$a[l; r] = a_l, a_{l + 1}, \dots, a_{r}$$$. Your task is to reverse such a subarray that the sum of elements on even positions of the resulting array is maximized (i. e. the sum of elements $$$a_0, a_2, \dots, a_{2k}$$$ for integer $$$k = \lfloor\frac{n-1}{2}\rfloor$$$ should be maximum possible). You have to answer $$$t$$$ independent test cases.
input_specification: The first line of the input contains one integer $$$t$$$ ($$$1 \le t \le 2 \cdot 10^4$$$) — the number of test cases. Then $$$t$$$ test cases follow. The first line of the test case contains one integer $$$n$$$ ($$$1 \le n \le 2 \cdot 10^5$$$) — the length of $$$a$$$. The second line of the test case contains $$$n$$$ integers $$$a_0, a_1, \dots, a_{n-1}$$$ ($$$1 \le a_i \le 10^9$$$), where $$$a_i$$$ is the $$$i$$$-th element of $$$a$$$. It is guaranteed that the sum of $$$n$$$ does not exceed $$$2 \cdot 10^5$$$ ($$$\sum n \le 2 \cdot 10^5$$$).
output_specification: For each test case, print the answer on the separate line — the maximum possible sum of elements on even positions after reversing at most one subarray (continuous subsegment) of $$$a$$$.
approach_summary: Apply Knapsack and Basic Dynamic Programming paradigm under the Dynamic Programming (DP) framework. Exploit problem invariants to reduce state space and achieve optimal complexity.
